title: Random walks in Dirichlet random environment in dimension $d+1$
authors: Guillaume Barraquand, Alexander K. Hartmann, Pierre Le Doussal
abstract: The atypical behaviour of random walks in time-dependent random environment was recently related to Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) growth. While this is now well-understood in spatial dimension $d=1$, further efforts are necessary to better understand these connections in dimensions $d>1$. In this paper, we study this problem numerically for $d=1, 2$ and $3$, focusing on a discrete model with Dirichlet distributed transition probabilities. This model is a generalization of an integrable model in $d=1$, and it has the advantage of admitting an explicit, product-form, stationary measure. We verify that the growth of the variance of the logarithm of point-to-point probabilities, namely from the origin to position $x$ in time $t$, is compatible with KPZ growth in dimension $d=1$ and $d=2$. In spatial dimension $d=3$, we confirm the existence of a phase transition as the angle $\vert x\vert /t$ increases and we obtain a lower bound based on an exact second moment calculation. We find that in the weak disorder phase the point-to-point probability acquires a heavy tailed distribution, and that in the strong disorder phase the cumulants of its logarithm grow with time. Further, we show that for this model, we can compute exactly the sample to sample variance of the thermal average $\overline{ \langle x \rangle^2}$ and that it is related to the extreme diffusion coefficient introduced recently.
summary: This paper studies random walks in a Dirichlet random environment, aiming to understand how their fluctuations relate to the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) growth universality class beyond $d=1$. Through numerical and analytical methods, it confirms KPZ scaling in lower dimensions, identifies phase transitions in higher dimensions, and derives exact formulas for key statistical quantities like the second moment.
main_problem: The paper investigates the atypical behavior of random walks in time-dependent random environments (RWRE), specifically linking its fluctuations to Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) growth, particularly in dimensions $d>1$. It also analyzes the asymptotic second moment of point-to-point probabilities.
main_result: The model confirms KPZ compatibility for variance growth in $d=1$ and $d=2$, identifies a phase transition in $d=3$, and provides an exact calculation for the sample-to-sample variance related to extreme diffusion coefficients.
method: The study employs numerical simulations across dimensions ($d=1, 2, 3$) combined with rigorous asymptotic analysis techniques, including second moment calculations and comparisons to continuum scaling limits.
model_or_system: The system is a random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{d+1}$ whose transition probabilities are governed by a Dirichlet distribution. This model generalizes known integrable models in $d=1$ and exhibits an explicit product-form stationary measure.
key_observables: Variance of the logarithm of point-to-point probabilities, the annealed drift $\langle X(t) angle$, the diffusion matrix $D$, and the second moment $m_2(v)$.
important_parameters: Spatial dimension $d$ (tested up to 3), time $t$, and the ratio $|x|/t$ which dictates phase transition behavior.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on numerical verification of scaling laws, asymptotic approximations for moments, and relating the system to known KPZ universality classes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the space-time trajectory of the random walk in $d=1+1$ embedded in $\mathbb{Z}^2$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the connection between RWRE and KPZ growth (numerical studies) to analyzing phase transitions ($d=3$), detailing the scaling laws for probability fluctuations ($\log P$), and concluding with an exact calculation of the second moment $m_2(v)$ in the weak disorder regime.
why_interesting: The deep connection between random walks, disordered media, and non-equilibrium growth phenomena like KPZ is central to modern statistical physics. The explicit treatment of higher dimensions ($d>1$) for this specific Dirichlet model provides crucial benchmarks against continuum theories.
